options.language_interference: real: one shared distribution must serve all 16; weaker languages risk dilution (documented in multilingual literature)

options.name: Shared foundation + language-specific adapters
options.training_complexity: moderate: shared pretraining + per-language SFT; 16 adapter lifecycles to version
options.maintainability: moderate: 17 artifacts (1 base + 16 adapters); rollback per adapter possible
options.cross_language_transfer: partial: shared trunk transfers; adapters memorize language-specific surface forms
options.language_interference: low: adapters isolate language-specific directions; dilution mostly avoided
options.local_deployment: good: base + 1/16th adapter per language; adapter load adds ~1.2 MB
options.checkpoint_compatibility: base reusable; adapters trained from scratch (no existing adapters)
options.ops_complexity: medium: adapter registry, routing/selection at inference, per-language eval
options.evidence_for: adapters are proven for parameter-efficient specialisation; inference cost barely changes
options.evidence_against: routing logic needed at inference (language detection); adapters cannot fix a weak shared trunk (we have one)
options.verdict: FALLBACK IF A's shared trunk shows destructive interference at scale; NOT FIRST CHOICE today

options.name: Shared foundation + language-family adapters
options.training_complexity: moderate: family assignment decisions (which language goes where); 8 adapters
options.maintainability: good: 9 artifacts; coarser specialisation than B
options.cross_language_transfer: high within family (C/C++/C#/Java transfer strongly); zero across distant families except through trunk
options.language_interference: low-medium: family adapters absorb broad regularities; individual languages still diluted within family
options.local_deployment: good: base + one family adapter; routing needs family detection
options.checkpoint_compatibility: base reusable; family adapters trained from scratch
options.evidence_for: family granularity matches known software ecosystems (Curly-brace C-family vs scripting vs FP vs SQL)
options.evidence_against: family assignment is judgement, not measurement; no family-annotated corpus exists here yet
options.verdict: VIABLE VARIANT OF B; useful if B's 16 adapters are operationally heavy; not proven either

options.name: Separate per-language models
options.training_complexity: highest: 16 independent runs, 16 data pools, 16 eval cycles
options.maintainability: poor: 16 model lifecycles; no shared capability; regression per language invisible to others
options.language_interference: none (each model isolated) — the only guaranteed isolation method, at maximal cost
options.local_deployment: poor: 1.84 GB total checkpoints; user must choose a model per language
options.checkpoint_compatibility: none shared; each trained separately; no reuse of this repo's verified pipeline gains
options.evidence_for: only valid when interference is proven severe at A scale AND per-language data suffices (none does today)
options.evidence_against: we cannot train even one competent model at 28.8M; 16 is absurd at current data/compute
options.verdict: REJECTED for now; keep as documented last-resort fallback

decision.scope: engineering implementation and local feasibility analysis only; no training, no data acquisition
reasons: a multilingual shared-model program is technically plausible (tokenizer is adequate for all 73 audited samples, no roundtrip loss)
BUT the qualified in-repo multilingual code supply is exactly 1.59M Python tokens and ZERO for every other language
and no multilingual benchmark-executed capability exists for any language (0/30 on Python; 0/16 on the multilingual starter)
and 10 of 16 L1.0 toolchains are locally usable but 4 (php/ruby/swift/dart) are not, and typescript has no compiler
and no architecture beyond the verified 28.8M baseline is justified by evidence today
owner_approvals_required_for_L0.6: written authorization to acquire licensed multilingual data (named corpora; legal sign-off per corpus)
written authorization for GPU compute budget (class and duration)
selection of the initial L1.0 language set to actually execute (subset of the 16 recommended by toolchain+data)
confirmation that the multilingual benchmark acceptance bar (>= 8/16 per language) is binding
decision on execution of TypeScript via Node type-stripping vs installing tsc (authorization required)
confirmation that L0.1 default checkpoint remains untouched
what_would_flip_to_GO: owner-authorized acquisition of >= 20B tokens of license-verified multilingual code with clean legal review
>= 24 GB VRAM-class compute for a >= 100M-parameter model, or equivalent CPU-only schedule accepted (~28 days)
a candidate passing >= 8/16 multilingual tasks AND beating the frozen Python bar on its own benchmark
what_would_flip_to_NO_GO: owner declines data acquisition or compute budget
legal review rejects all candidate corpora for the selected languages
an authorized L0.6 experiment scores 0/16 across all languages with a clean benchmark
